featured.title: TPT-Finder bioimpedance instrument (BioZ v4)
text: TPT-Finder is a pen-like multisensing surgical instrument meant to tell thyroid from parathyroid tissue in real time during surgery. I designed its tetrapolar bioimpedance board, BioZ v4 (AD5933, INA333, AD8606 Howland current source). On an earlier board, BioZ v2, I calibrated the sensing chain to 0.034% error at 33 kHz (2200 Ω calibration). I ran the ex-vivo study and all 500+ tissue measurements. My role: Biomedical Instrumentation & Impedance Lead.

featured.title: Project SHIELD: sensor DAQ board and stress-test rig
text: An ESP32-S3 data-acquisition board for a design with 8 sensor types, plus the rig that stress-tests it. On the capstone I was co-hardware lead (with Thomas Glass) and procurement lead. I designed and built the Faraday cage for the EMI tests and wrote the automation for the orbital-shaker vibration rig, and at ARC Lab I lead the undergraduate team running the stress-test campaign.

featured.title: BackOnTrack: wearable posture monitor
text: A wearable posture monitor: an ESP32-S3 with BNO085 IMUs for the upper and lower back and a MyoWare 2.0 EMG sensor on the upper trapezius, as the team's user manual describes it. It was a four-person EE/BIOEN 461 course team, and I wrote all of the firmware (15/15 commits): modular FreeRTOS/ESP-IDF code and a real-time rule-based classifier (good posture + 5 fault states with the one IMU the public firmware runs). Checked against real-time movements, its classification was 95.3% accurate.

featured.title: SmartCrib: on-device infant cry detector
text: Joint project with Jonathan Lu. PDM microphone → MFCC → an INT8 TensorFlow Lite Micro model running fully on an Arduino Nano 33 BLE Sense (Cortex-M4), with an ESP32 alert bridge over BLE. Built as the EE/CSE 474 final project.

featured.title: Real-time EMG BCI
text: I built a real-time EMG cursor BCI end to end: EMG streaming, a Kalman-filter closed-loop cursor, and a feedback-lag sweep.

*Built for EE 466 (Winter 2026) at UW in a three-person lab group with Jonathan and Olivia, following the course protocol and script outlines by A. L. Orsborn. The code here and the lag-sweep analysis are my own.*
